request.state: Consider package composition for a proposed business language, before any compiler/runtime implementation. A company can run physical mail with an externally reviewed purchase, no linked membership term and no invoice fees, while still needing notification, authorized collection, frozen forwarding instructions, evidenced dispatch/return and retained private handling history. Nevertheless plain symbol imports currently install whole owners. Verified closure contains ten owners and nine service-binding keys: email, billing, membership ingress, payments, billing ingress, documents, sales ingress, qualified sales and commissions. Charge is a structural value that can come from the existing bound invoice interface. The customer package imports a finance role from the invoice owner. More substantially Mail reads a live membership Term and a pure eligibility function whose truth depends on present payment, customer/seat grants, suspension/revocation and interval. That record/function dependency includes membership and its referral/affiliate dependencies; manual runtime choices cannot statically erase it. Interfaces alone carry extracted schemas and do not install provider execution. Every model/rule/CRUD has exactly one owner; another package cannot patch its records. Integrated Mail must still handle paid terms and unique frozen fees, uncertain invoices and reconciliation, trusted correlation, privacy and current authorization, without equating invoice success to parcel dispatch. Proposed contracts can change freely but may not duplicate types, add wrapper/build files or pretend unproved pruning is safe. Outstanding deliveries and schedules use pinned provider identities and must be retained/reconciled/drained before removal, including old uncertain work. No executed performance/cost or semantic-analysis proof is supplied.

closure.instructions: Choose the smallest coherent direction against equal manual and integrated outcomes, accounting for setup burden, explicit source and new semantic responsibility.

criteria.whole: Leave whole-owner inference and required bindings intact and publish an accurate install plan. All current owners, hooks and provider work survive and no new construct is needed; standalone manual/no-fee mail still carries the unused commercial installations.
criteria.values: Restrict owner-free imports to canonical structural values and static role identities, following their schema/label dependencies. Use the bound invoice schema for Charge. Stateful functions and model references still include their entire executable owner. This reduces accidental execution edges but cannot remove live-term closure or the independently declared billing service.
criteria.partition: Use explicit optional workflow packages and current canonical owner exports/events for a real commercial/core split. Preserve each stored model and all authority in its existing owner and implement admitted integration handoffs rather than cross-package writes. It can reduce provider closure if the full handoff is made equivalent, but requires additional boundaries and business bridges; a proven complete partition is not available from the present source.
criteria.optional: Introduce a single authored app-level list of existing deployment binding keys that may be unconfigured, without removing any executable declaration. Unlisted keys remain mandatory. All schemas and owner authorization/hook behavior remain installed; a missing listed target causes atomic rule_failed with no domain or delivery commit when a send is attempted, never a synthetic completion. Manual/no-fee paths avoid those sends; integrated deployment supplies the providers. Removing a binding is forbidden while old unresolved namespace-bound work remains, under the existing release/drain boundary. This trades one explicit deployment contract for fewer unused adapters and avoids new mutating-owner bridges, while retaining the large source graph.
